"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:367 -- a sparse "chat-turn / Arabic conjunction" detector.

What it does, in plain terms (its prediction is the component's contribution at each token):
  * `<|im_start|>` that opens a chat turn (after a newline) -> about +1.25. The same token
    right after `<|endoftext|>` (first turn of a packed document) -> about -0.3.
  * Arabic-script conjunction "و" (wa, "and") that starts a word -> about +2.5, and about +5
    when it follows a comma or a line break. Arabic particles ف (fa), ل (li), ب (bi), ك (ka)
    as word-initial tokens -> about +0.9.
  * Persian text switches all Arabic rules off (Persian uses the same letter و but the
    component stays silent there). Persian is detected from its letters ی ک گ پ چ ژ seen so
    far in the document.
  * A run of middle dots "··" (leader dots) -> about -1.1.
  * Katakana/hiragana small tsu ッ / っ -> about -2.5.
  * Everything else -> 0.

The carry is one flag: whether the current document has shown Persian-only letters.
"""

READS = ()

PERSIAN_LETTERS = set("یکگپچژ")
ARABIC_PARTICLES = ("ف", "ل", "ب", "ك")
CLAUSE_BREAKS = (",", "،", "\n", "|")


def _is_arabic(text):
    return any("؀" <= c <= "ۿ" for c in text)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    persian = False if new_doc else bool(carry)
    if any(c in PERSIAN_LETTERS for c in tok):
        persian = True

    if tok == "<|im_start|>":
        return persian, (-0.3 if prev == "<|endoftext|>" else 1.25)
    if tok == "··":
        return persian, -1.1
    if tok in ("ッ", "っ"):
        return persian, -2.5
    if _is_arabic(tok) and not persian:
        first = tok.lstrip(" ")[:1]
        word_start = tok.startswith(" ") or not _is_arabic(prev[-1:])
        if first == "و" and word_start:
            after_break = prev.endswith(CLAUSE_BREAKS) or tok == "و"
            return persian, (5.0 if after_break else 2.5)
        if tok.startswith(" ") and first in ARABIC_PARTICLES:
            return persian, 0.9
    return persian, 0.0

"""Layer 1, MLP down-projection unit 369: a document-start unit.

What it does: it is negative on the first token of every document. Where a document
begins, the model resets attention and positions, so that first token sees only itself,
and the unit writes a fixed, token-dependent offset there. The offset is about -0.4 for
most first tokens (capitalised words, code and markup symbols, punctuation, digits,
non-Latin text), about -0.7 for a lone capital letter (R, P, I), and only about -0.2 for a
lowercase English-style word with a leading space (" model", " small"). Every later
position is essentially silent (values within about +-0.05).

Row starts count as document starts, as they do in the model (positions restart there).
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

START_WORD = -0.20      # first token is a lowercase word with a leading space
START_CAPITAL = -0.70   # first token is a single capital letter
START_OTHER = -0.40     # any other first token of a document
MID_DOCUMENT = 0.0      # every later position


def is_space_word(token: str) -> bool:
    """A lowercase word with a leading space, e.g. ' model'."""
    return len(token) > 1 and token[0] == " " and token[1:].isalpha() and token[1:].islower()


def is_lone_capital(token: str) -> bool:
    """A single capital letter, with or without a leading space."""
    return len(token.strip()) == 1 and token.strip().isupper()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    first = len(docs) == 1 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]
    if not first:
        return None, MID_DOCUMENT
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if is_space_word(token):
        return None, START_WORD
    if is_lone_capital(token):
        return None, START_CAPITAL
    return None, START_OTHER

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:371: a weak, sparse component.

What it does, in plain terms:
  * Fires (positive) on long runs of one repeated symbol used as a visual rule or
    separator: "--------", "========", "########", "////////", "________", "~~~~~~".
    Shorter runs ("--", "==") are about zero.
  * Fires on markdown/code block markers: the code fence ``` and a few
    code/diff markers (@@ hunk headers, @Override, namespace, EOF heredoc).
  * Sits slightly negative on the first token of each document (the token right
    after <|endoftext|>, or the first token of a row), where it is also noisy.
  * Strongly negative on the middle-dot leader token ·· (rare).
Everything else is predicted as 0. Most of the activation's variance is small
noise on ordinary tokens, which these concepts do not capture.
"""

READS = ()

RULE_CHARS = set("-=_*~#/^.")
FENCE = ("```", " ```")
MARKERS = ("@@", " @@", "@Override", "namespace", "EOF")


def run_length(text):
    """Length of the text if it is one symbol repeated (ignoring spaces), else 0."""
    s = text.strip()
    if s and len(set(s)) == 1 and s[0] in RULE_CHARS:
        return len(s)
    return 0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, -0.15  # first token of a document
    if tok == "··":
        return None, -2.4  # middle-dot leader
    n = run_length(tok)
    if n >= 5:
        return None, 0.5  # long separator line
    if n >= 3:
        return None, 0.1
    if tok in FENCE:
        return None, 0.5  # code block fence
    if tok in MARKERS:
        return None, 0.6  # diff / heredoc / annotation markers
    return None, 0.0

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:373, version 3: deliberation / planning words, graded.

Fires (positive) on Chinese words for thinking something over or planning it.
The strongest cases in the harvest are the "consider / worry" morphemes
(考虑, 考慮, 虑, 慮: activations about 2 to 4.5); the planning, method and
strategy words (计, 計, 办法, 辦法, 采取, 略, 预计) are weaker (about 0.5 to 1.4).
The program predicts those two levels on those tokens and 0 everywhere else.
It does not predict the component's negative activations (on the U+FFFD
byte-fragment tokens), whose sign it cannot tell from the token.
"""

READS = ()

STRONG = frozenset(["考虑", "考虑到", "考慮", "虑", "慮"])
WEAK = frozenset(["计", "計", "预计", "办法", "辦法", "采取", "略"])


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token in STRONG:
        return None, 2.5
    if token in WEAK:
        return None, 1.0
    return None, 0.0

Negative responses are strongest for null checks, types in brackets, and
familiar library members. Bare word pieces and ordinary prose are weaker.
Only the current and previous token are used; state resets at document
boundaries. There are also small rules for node_modules and middle dots.
This is a lexical approximation, not a parser or a complete list of APIs.

import math
import builtins

        'None': -.9, 'nullptr': -1., 'undefined': -.4}

    'int': (-1.2, -1.5, -.4), 'uint': (-1.2, -1.5, -.4),
    'float': (-.8, -1.5, -.4), 'double': (-.65, -1.5, -.4),
    'bool': (-1., -.8, -.7), 'boolean': (-1., -.8, -.7),
    'byte': (-.7, -1., -.3), 'char': (-.7, -1., -.3),

    'String': (-1.6, -3.2, -.4), 'void': (-1., -1.5, -.7),

    ('ArrayList HashMap HashSet LinkedList StringBuilder', -2., -4.3),
    ('DataFrame Series ndarray array arange linspace zeros ones randn tensor',
     -.1, -1.6),

    ('getElementById querySelector querySelectorAll createElement appendChild',

    ('list dict tuple set List Dict Tuple Set Array Map Vec Box Option Result',

    ('np numpy pd pandas matplotlib pyplot', -.6, -1.6),
    ('sys os shutil datetime stdlib stdio heapq subprocess threading strconv',
     -.35, -.7),

API = {word: (plain, dotted) for words, plain, dotted in FAMILIES

NAMESPACES = set('std np numpy pd pandas matplotlib pyplot sys os io fmt '
                 'console System java javax util datetime collections typing'.split())
STANDARD_NAMES = set(dir(str)) | set(dir(math)) | set(dir(builtins))

       '+=': -.8, '-=': -.65, '*=': -.6, '/=': -.4,
       '&&': -.4, '||': -.3, '=>': -.4, '<<': -.4, '>>': -.2}

        elif word in ('cout', 'cerr', 'cin', 'endl'):

"""Approximate an O-sensitive, negative-going text feature.

Short O-bearing fragments respond most strongly, especially at their start
and in capitals. Common grammatical words weaken this signal; an O in an
unfinished word can affect later fragments. There are extra responses to zero,
whitespace widths two modulo four, initial words, and the colon in an initial
'Title:' field.
"""
import codecs
import math
import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency
import inflect

READS = ()
GRAMMAR = set((
    'to of for from on or into onto upon you your yours yourself '
    'yourselves our ours ourselves who whom whose how some someone '
    'somebody something anyone everyone none nothing not only both '
    'those more most also could would should'
).split())
_number_names = inflect.engine()
NUMBER_WORDS = {
    _number_names.number_to_words(n)
    for n in list(range(21)) + list(range(30, 101, 10))
    + [1000, 10**6, 10**9, 10**12]
}
PARTICLES = set('のをもと')

@lru_cache(None)
def romanize(s):
    # Do not mistake Han dictionary readings for letters printed on the page.
    if any('CJK' in unicodedata.name(c, '') for c in s):
        return ''
    return anyascii(s.replace('و', 'o')).lower()

@lru_cache(None)
def local_value(s):
    raw = s.strip()
    roman = romanize(raw)
    letters = ''.join(c for c in roman if c.isalpha())
    value = -0.025
    grammatical = (s[:1].isspace() and roman in (GRAMMAR | NUMBER_WORDS))
    if grammatical or raw in PARTICLES:
        value -= 0.024
    elif 'o' in letters:
        length = max(1, sum(c.isalpha() for c in raw))
        common = (max(0, zipf_frequency(raw.lower(), 'en') - 4)
                  if raw.isascii() and raw.isalpha() else 0)
        value -= 0.311 + 0.597 / math.sqrt(length)
        value += 0.032 * min(length, 15)
        value -= 0.486 * letters.startswith('o')
        value -= 0.211 * (len(letters) > 1 and letters[1] == 'o')
        value -= 0.293 * raw.isupper()
        value -= 0.152 * raw.istitle()
        value += 0.096 * ('ou' in letters)
        value += 0.064 * common
    if raw in ('0', '０'):
        value -= 1.45
    spaces = s.rstrip('\r\n').replace('\t', '')
    if spaces and not spaces.strip() and len(spaces) % 4 == 2:
        value -= 1.762
        value += 0.745 * ('\n' in s)
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        word, position, title, pending = '', 0, False, b''
    else:
        _, word, position, title, pending = carry
    data = pending + prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    s, used = codecs.utf_8_decode(data, 'replace', False)
    pending = data[used:]
    raw = s.strip()
    value = local_value(s)
    if word and s[:1].isalpha() and 'o' in word:
        distance = len(word) - word.rfind('o') - 1
        value -= 0.625 / (1 + distance)
    if position == 0 and raw.isalpha() and not s[:1].isspace():
        value -= 0.563
    if position == 1 and title and s == ':':
        value -= 15.252
    if position == 0:
        title = raw == 'Title'
    if s and not s[:1].isalpha():
        word = ''
    for c in s:
        roman = romanize(c)
        if c.isalpha() and roman:
            word = (word + roman)[-40:]
        else:
            word = ''
    return (doc, word, position + 1, title, pending), value

    the token alone, but no short list of tokens captures that, so they are predicted 0.

about 22%, but it has no concept behind it, so it is not used here.

    "namespace package include main var let function".split()

reference numeral such as "interface  132 " in patent text. Everywhere else it is near 0.

PAREN_AFTER_CITE = 0.7  # " (" right after ")" or "]"
BRACKET_RUN = 0.4       # "][" between citation numbers, as in [23][24]

WEAK = frozenset("ts tsx js jsx py rs java git yaml css cjs mjs scss".split())

STRONG = 1.2  # typical activation on a name in NAMES
WEAK_VALUE = 0.5


def _word(prefix):
    """The word the newest token ends, lowercased: letters, digits and underscores, joined
    across tokens back to the first character that is not one of them."""
    word = ""
    for s in reversed(prefix.token_strings):
        m = re.search(r"[A-Za-z0-9_]*$", s)
        word = m.group(0) + word
        if m.start() > 0 or not s:
            break
    return word.lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = _word(prefix)
    if word in NAMES:
        return carry, STRONG
    if word == "go":
        # "go" as the Go command in code ("&& go test", "    go build"), not "to go"
        previous = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""
        if not previous[-1:].isalpha():
            return carry, STRONG
    if word in WEAK:
        return carry, WEAK_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""A phrase-ending approximation.

A small lexical heuristic for familiar phrase completions. It recognizes a few
productive English constructions, dictionary compounds, time/space noun phrases,
and possessive body-part phrases. Chinese words spanning tokens receive small
bonuses, with a larger bonus for dictionary-labelled idioms. Hexadecimal letters
and digits in identifier-like runs are a separate positive case. Constants were
estimated on training text; this does not reproduce all contextual variation.
"""
from functools import lru_cache
import re
import regex
import wordnet
import cedict

READS = ()
ARTICLES = {'a', 'an', 'the'}
POSSESSIVES = {'my', 'your', 'his', 'her', 'its', 'our', 'their'}
TIME = {'time', 'times', 'day', 'days', 'night', 'nights', 'year', 'years',
        'week', 'weeks', 'month', 'months', 'hour', 'hours', 'minute',
        'minutes', 'second', 'seconds', 'moment', 'moments', 'while'}
SPACE = {'way', 'ways', 'road', 'roads', 'path', 'paths', 'place', 'places',
         'side', 'sides', 'end', 'ends', 'world', 'room', 'floor', 'door',
         'ground', 'air', 'space', 'home', 'sky'}
PREPOSITIONS = {'in', 'on', 'at', 'to', 'from', 'for', 'of', 'by', 'with',
                'into', 'under', 'over', 'through', 'across', 'around', 'down'}
STRONG_GRAMMAR = re.compile(
 r'(?:or not|(?:first|last) time|(?:as|than) (?:possible|usual|expected)|'
 r'from time to time|ahead of time|once upon a time)$', re.I)
BASIC_PHRASES = re.compile(
 r'(?:the way|a while|a time|the day|the night|other night|'
 r'(?:my|your|his|her|our|their) (?:life|way)|'
 r'than (?:that|ever|before)|(?:anything|something|nothing|anyone|everyone) else|'
 r'(?:the time has|yet to|more to) come)$', re.I)


@lru_cache(100000)
def categories(word):
    return wordnet.categories(word)

@lru_cache(100000)
def phrase(word):
    return wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)

@lru_cache(100000)
def chinese(word):
    glosses = cedict.glosses(word)
    return bool(glosses), any('idiom' in g for g in glosses)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    raw = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else b''
    previous = raw.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    new = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    s = new.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    raw = (raw + new)[-400:]
    text = raw.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')[-100:]
    value = 0.000

    # Hex fragments, including hyphenated identifiers such as UUIDs.
    run = re.search(r'(?:0[xX])?[0-9a-fA-F-]+$', previous)
    if run:
        r = run[0]
        length = len(r.replace('-', ''))
        if length >= 3 and any(ch.isdigit() for ch in r):
            if re.fullmatch('-?[a-fA-F]+', s):
                value += 0.739 + 0.761*(length >= 8)
            if s.isdigit() and re.search('[a-fA-F]', r):
                value += 0.111 + 0.149*(length >= 8)

    if re.search('[A-Za-z]$', text):
        tail = re.search(r'[A-Za-z]+(?:[ -]+[A-Za-z]+)*$', text)[0]
        words = re.findall('[A-Za-z]+', tail.lower())
        w = words[-1]
        p = words[-2] if len(words) > 1 else ''
        if s[:1].isspace() and s.strip().isascii() and s.strip().isalpha():
            determined = p in ARTICLES | POSSESSIVES
            preposition = p in PREPOSITIONS
            if w in TIME:
                value += 0.039 + 0.135*determined
                value += 0.080*preposition
            if w in SPACE:
                value += 0.034 + 0.140*determined
                value += 0.023*preposition
            if 'noun.body' in categories(w):
                value += 0.037*determined
                value += 0.287*(p in POSSESSIVES)
        kinds = set()
        long_phrase = False
        for n in range(2, min(5, len(words)+1)):
            entry = phrase(' '.join(words[-n:]))
            kinds.update(entry)
            long_phrase |= bool(entry) and n >= 3
        value += 0.017*('noun' in kinds)
        value += 0.033*('verb' in kinds)
        value += 0.025*('adjective' in kinds)
        value += 0.062*('adverb' in kinds)
        value += 0.145*long_phrase
        value += 0.801*bool(STRONG_GRAMMAR.search(text))
        value += 0.235*bool(BASIC_PHRASES.search(text))

    # Only entries crossing the current token boundary count here.
    if regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}$', text):
        tail = regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}+$', text)[0]
        token_tail = regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}+$', s)
        newlen = len(token_tail[0]) if token_tail else 1
        lengths = set()
        idiom = False
        for n in range(max(2, newlen+1), min(7, len(tail)+1)):
            known, labelled_idiom = chinese(tail[-n:])
            if known: lengths.add(min(n, 4))
            idiom |= labelled_idiom
        value += 0.059*(2 in lengths)
        value += 0.080*(3 in lengths)
        value += 0.151*(4 in lengths)
        value += 0.863*idiom
    return (doc, raw), float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj, component 382: a sparse detector for hex-string letters and for
nouns that close common idioms.

Plain terms. The component is quiet almost everywhere; its activation is signed and mostly
small, and its large positive events are rare. This program predicts those events:
- Hex strings. A lowercase letter a-f inside a run of hexadecimal characters (a git hash,
  a UUID, a memory address, a 0x... constant) pushes the component strongly positive.
  'f' is strongest (about 2.1), then 'e' (1.6), 'c' and 'b' (1.25), 'a' and 'd' (about 0.9).
  Digits 0-9 do not fire. A "hex run" means at least 8 hex characters in the 12 tokens
  before the letter, in the same document.
- Idiom nouns. Common nouns that often finish a fixed phrase ("the night", "my face",
  "from time to time", "the way", "a piece", "their minds") get a moderate value, 0.2.
- Possessive nouns. A word right after my, his, her, their, your or its gets 0.1.
- The first token of each row, the model's first position, gets 0.26.
Everything else is predicted as 0.

The values are rough averages measured on training text, not fitted to the eval rows.
The program explains only a few percent of the variance: most of the component's activation
is small and diffuse, and the large events are scattered over many contexts.
"""

READS = ()

HEX = set("0123456789abcdef")
LETTER_VALUE = {"f": 2.1, "e": 1.6, "c": 1.25, "b": 1.25, "a": 0.9, "d": 0.8}
POSSESSIVES = {" my", " his", " her", " their", " your", " its"}
IDIOM_NOUNS = {
    " night", " face", " mind", " mouth", " head", " life", " lives", " eye", " eyes",
    " day", " time", " way", " light", " dark", " box", " piece", " pieces", " away",
    " sea", " road", " moment", " reason", " circle", " heart", " end", " side", " home",
    " air", " field", " floor", " room",
}
FIRST_TOKEN_VALUE = 0.26
IDIOM_NOUN_VALUE = 0.2
POSSESSIVE_NOUN_VALUE = 0.1


def _is_hex_piece(s):
    return len(s) > 0 and all(ch in HEX for ch in s)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    if prefix.position == 0:
        return None, FIRST_TOKEN_VALUE
    s = strings[-1]
    # hex letter inside a hex string
    if _is_hex_piece(s) and any(ch in "abcdef" for ch in s):
        chars = 0
        doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
        for i in range(max(0, len(strings) - 13), len(strings) - 1):
            if prefix.document_ids[i] == doc and _is_hex_piece(strings[i]):
                chars += len(strings[i])
        if chars >= 8:
            return None, LETTER_VALUE.get(s, 1.0)
    if s in IDIOM_NOUNS:
        return None, IDIOM_NOUN_VALUE
    if len(strings) > 1 and strings[-2] in POSSESSIVES and s.startswith(" ") and s[1:].isalpha():
        return None, POSSESSIVE_NOUN_VALUE
    return None, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""A partial detector of old-fashioned spelling and elision.

Long s, clipped -ing endings, and short-word apostrophes predict positive
activations. A Latin Extended-A lead byte is an early, ambiguous long-s
clue. These clues and archaic function words raise sensitivity for the
rest of the document. In that context, also score word fragments that
become more frequent after historical spelling changes. Otherwise the
prediction is nearly zero; much token-specific variation is not modeled.
"""
import regex as re
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
LANGUAGES = ('en', 'de', 'fr', 'it', 'es')
ARCHAIC = {
    'thou', 'thee', 'thy', 'thine', 'ye', 'hath', 'doth', 'shalt',
    'wilt', 'unto', 'whilst', 'ere', 'nay', 'saith', 'quoth', 'tis',
    'twas', 'twere', 'art',
}

@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def frequency(word):
    if not word:
        return 0.0
    return max(zipf_frequency(word, lang) for lang in LANGUAGES)

@lru_cache(maxsize=100000)
def restoration_gain(word):
    word = word.lower()
    variants = {word.replace('ſ', 's')}
    for old, new in [('f', 's'), ('v', 'u'), ('u', 'v'),
                     ('y', 'i'), ('i', 'j')]:
        variants.add(word.replace(old, new))
    for ending, replacement in [('e', ''), ('eth', 's'),
                                 ('est', ''), ('in', 'ing')]:
        if word.endswith(ending):
            variants.add(word[:-len(ending)] + replacement)
    return max(frequency(w) - frequency(word) for w in variants)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', False, b'', False)
    _, word, archaic, previous_bytes, code = carry
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    raw = prefix.token_bytes[-1]
    before = '' if text[:1].isspace() else word
    match = re.search(r'[^\W\d_]+$', text)
    if match:
        word = (before if match.start() == 0 else '') + match.group()
    else:
        word = ''
    long_s = 'ſ' in text or b'\xc5\xbf' in previous_bytes[-1:] + raw
    lead = raw.endswith(b'\xc5')
    tail = raw.startswith(b'\xbf') and previous_bytes.endswith(b'\xc5')
    quote = text.strip() in ("'", '’', '᾽')
    if '\n' in text:
        code = False
    code = code or any(c in text for c in '_{}')
    short_elision = quote and 0 < len(before) <= 3 and not code
    # Colloquial spellings such as talkin'.
    ing_elision = quote and before.lower().endswith('in')
    letters = text.strip()
    latin = bool(re.fullmatch(r'\p{Script=Latin}+', letters))

    value = -0.001
    value += 1.0 * long_s + 2.75 * tail + 1.1 * lead
    value += short_elision * (0.3 + 2.0 * archaic)
    value += 2.1 * ing_elision
    if archaic and latin:
        value += 0.03
        gain = restoration_gain(word) if word else 0.0
        value += 0.5 * min(1.0, max(0.0, gain - 1.0))

    archaic = archaic or word.lower() in ARCHAIC or long_s or lead
    return (doc, word, archaic, raw, code), float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""Layer 1 MLP down_proj, component 383: a dialect and old-spelling detector.

What it responds to: non-standard spellings of the kind found in dialect speech and
old-fashioned print. Its activation is small and sign-varying almost everywhere, and
large on a few kinds of token:
  - an elided apostrophe: an apostrophe directly after a clipped word stub, as in
    o' (of), livin' and tellin' (-ing), n', de' (Italian/French elision). After "o" or a
    word ending in "in" it is strongest; after other stubs of one or two letters it is
    moderate;
  - the long s "ſ" of old German and English print (theſe, daſs).
Ordinary words, possessives, quotation marks, code and punctuation are predicted as 0;
there the activation is near zero. The values are rounded from the mean activations of
each kind on a small sample of training text, so they are rough. The program explains
only the largest spikes: most of the component's variance is small noise it does not
capture.
"""

READS = ()

LONG_S = "ſ"
APOSTROPHE = "'"
STUB_MAX = 2  # a clipped stub has at most this many letters
ELISION_VALUE = 4.0  # o', livin', tellin'
STUB_VALUE = 0.6  # other short stubs: L', d', n', de'
LONG_S_VALUE = 1.4


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = 0.0
    if len(prefix) > 1:
        prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
        stub = prev.lstrip()
        if tok == APOSTROPHE and prev[-1:].isalpha():
            if stub == "o" or stub.endswith("in"):
                value = ELISION_VALUE
            elif len(stub) <= STUB_MAX:
                value = STUB_VALUE
    if LONG_S in tok:
        value = LONG_S_VALUE
    return None, value
